reports.title: UNAUDITED CONDENSED CONSOLIDATED INTERIM FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

lines: Our capital expenditures for 2025 were approximately $283.7 million, and our capital expenditures for 2026 are expected to be approximately $400.0 million.

desk.headline: Revenue up 24% to $2.17bn and adjusted EPS $0.42, both beat; full-year 2026 outlook raised and $1.0bn buyback approved

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted diluted; IFRS diluted EPS $0.41 vs $0.25

results: Revenue jumped 24% (23% in constant currency) to $2.17bn, ahead of the $2.14bn estimate; adjusted EPS rose to $0.42 from $0.33.
Salomon's Outdoor Performance unit grew 27% and Arc'teryx's Technical Apparel 26%; Wilson's Ball & Racquet grew 12% but its margin slipped.
Adjusted gross margin rose 1.5 points to 59.4% and adjusted operating margin rose 0.7 points to 16.4%.
Greater China grew 30% and Asia Pacific 48%; direct-to-consumer sales rose 36% to $982.6m.
Debt is now minimal after the March share sale repaid the $800m notes; the board approved a $1.0bn buyback with no expiry date.

guidance.summary: Amer Sports raised its 2026 outlook: revenue growth of 25–26% (from about 24%) and adjusted EPS of $1.32–1.35 (from $1.27–1.30). For 2027 it expects growth around the middle of its long-term range of low double digits to mid-teens.

items.new: midpoint of low-double-digit to mid-teens range

points: Management reported a strong start to Q4 and expects Q4 revenue growth of 17–20% against a tough 29% comparison.
Arc'teryx's women's range is its fastest-growing category; the US is seen as the brand's biggest long-term opportunity.
Salomon is pushing into US premium sneaker shops and plans 8–9 new US stores.
China was called a challenging market overall, yet sales there grew 30%; Europe was also described as tough.
The new buyback will offset share dilution from staff incentive plans, with extra purchases if the share price looks too low. Guidance assumes current tariff rates hold.
call.source: Call coverage: Investing.com call transcript, 17 Nov 2026; figures from the press release (Exhibit 99.1)

watch: Whether Q4 revenue lands in the 17–20% growth range management talked about.
Pace of buybacks under the new $1.0bn programme.
China demand and any change in US tariffs.
